results.name: Dumbbell Alternate Biceps Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended by your sides and palms facing inwards.

Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl the right dumbbell towards your shoulder by contracting your biceps. Rotate your forearm as you lift the dumbbell so that your palm faces your shoulder at the top of the movement.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left arm while keeping the right arm extended. Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows stationary and close to your torso to isolate the biceps.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the dumbbells.
Breathe out as you curl the dumbbell up and breathe in as you lower it.
results.description: Dumbbell Alternate Biceps Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Hammer Curl (Back Supported)
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your torso. Let your arms hang straight down by your sides.
Keep your elbows close to your body and curl the right dumbbell towards your shoulder by bending your elbow. Keep your palm facing inward throughout the movement.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement with your left arm while keeping the right arm extended. Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms throughout the exercise.
Focus on using your biceps to lift the weight, avoiding any swinging or using momentum.
Breathe out as you curl the dumbbell up and breathe in as you lower it.
results.description: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Hammer Curl (Back Supported) is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl With Overhead Extension on Stability Ball
instructions: Kneel on a stability ball with your forefeet on the floor for support. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with one arm extended overhead and the other arm hanging by your side.

Simultaneously perform a bicep curl with the arm hanging by your side, bending your elbow to lift the dumbbell towards your shoulder and an overhead triceps extension with the other arm, bending your elbow to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Slowly return both arms to the starting position, ensuring control and stability throughout the movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain balance on the stability ball by engaging your core muscles throughout the exercise.
Perform the movements slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Keep your elbows close to your body during the bicep curl and ensure your overhead arm remains stable during the triceps extension.
results.description: Dumbbell Biceps Curl With Overhead Extension on Stability Ball is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Close-Grip Simultaneous Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a close grip, palms facing front.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl the dumbbells simultaneously towards your shoulders by contracting your biceps.
Pause at the top of the movement, squeezing your biceps.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows stationary and close to your body throughout the exercise to isolate the biceps.
Avoid swinging the weights or using momentum to lift the dumbbells.
Focus on a slow and controlled movement to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Dumbbell Close-Grip Simultaneous Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Cross Body Hammer Curl (Version 2)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended and palms facing your body.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the right dumbbell across your body towards your left shoulder, squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Repeat the movement with your left arm, curling the dumbbell towards your right shoulder. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your body and avoid swinging your arms to ensure maximum biceps engagement.
Maintain a neutral grip with your palms facing inwards throughout the exercise.
Focus on a controlled, steady movement to avoid using momentum.
results.description: Dumbbell Cross Body Hammer Curl (Version 2) is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Curl Alternating
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inwards (neutral grip).
Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl one dumbbell up towards your shoulder, rotating your wrist so your palm faces upward (supinated grip) at the top of the curl.
Hold the top position for a brief moment, ensuring you squeeze your biceps, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, rotating your wrist back to the neutral grip.
Repeat the curl with the other arm, alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movements in a controlled manner, avoiding any jerking or swinging.
Ensure your elbows stay close to your body and do not flare out during the curl.
Keep your wrists straight and avoid excessive bending.
results.description: Dumbbell Curl Alternating is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Curls
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing inwards (neutral grip).
Keep your elbows close to your torso and curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders, rotating your wrists so your palms face upward at the top of the curl.
Hold the top position for a brief moment, ensuring you squeeze your biceps.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, rotating your wrists back to the neutral grip, maintaining control throughout the movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movements in a controlled manner, avoiding any jerking or swinging.
Ensure your elbows stay close to your body and do not flare out during the curl.
Keep your wrists straight and avoid excessive bending.
results.description: Dumbbell Curls is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Drag Over Shoulder Bicep Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended down by your sides.
Begin the movement by curling the dumbbells up towards your shoulders while dragging your elbows backward, keeping them close to your body.
Once the dumbbells are close to your shoulders, push them up slowly to pass the shoulders.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a slow and controlled motion, avoiding any swinging or momentum.
Exhale as you curl the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them back down.
Keep your elbows close to your body throughout the movement to focus the effort on your biceps.
results.description: Dumbbell Drag Over Shoulder Bicep Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Half Biceps Curl for 21s
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward. Start with your arms fully extended by your sides.
Curl the dumbbells upward until your elbows are at a 90-degree angle, stopping halfway up. Hold for a brief moment.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with a controlled motion.
Repeat this half curl motion for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid swinging your body or using momentum to lift the weights.
Exhale as you curl the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
results.description: Dumbbell Half Biceps Curl for 21s is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl Simultaneous Arms
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip (palms facing your torso). Let your arms hang straight down at your sides.
Simultaneously curl both dumbbells upward towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, focusing on engaging your biceps and forearms.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring the dumbbells reach shoulder height.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum; focus on a controlled motion.
Keep your back straight and core engaged to prevent swaying.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to reduce strain on your joints.
results.description: Dumbbell Hammer Curl Simultaneous Arms is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.
